newsitem.title: FRANCE: Europe's AI(R) still studying 70-seat jet project.
newsitem.headline: Europe's AI(R) still studying 70-seat jet project.

text.p: European aircraft marketing consortium Aero International (Regional) said on Tuesday it was still studying the business case for launching a $1 billion 70-seat passenger jet and no decision had yet been taken.

"No decision has been taken. We are in the business evaluation phase", a company spokesman said. There has been industry talk that the project might be dropped as it was not commercially viable. "We are optimistic for a good end to the story," the spokesman said.
AI(R) consists of Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, and Alenia of Italy's Finmecanicca.

As part of the evaluation process, AI(R) is talking to airlines and potential industrial partners for the plane, which could be priced at $21-$22 million, making it $1-$2 million cheaper than the rival Canadair 700 product from Bombardier of Canada.
A series of board meetings is planned between now and the June 14 start of the Paris Le Bourget air show, to consider the launch decision and pricing, the spokesman said.
Industry sources said AI(R) is talking to Sweden's Saab and Casa of Spain as potential industrial partners.
AI(R) last month signed a non-exclusive memorandum of understanding with the KCDC group of South Korean companies interested in joining the project as industrial partners.
The Korean Commercial Aircraft Development Consortium is led by Samsung Aerospace Industries Co and includes Korean Air Lines Co, Daewoo Heavy Industries Co and Hyundai Space and Aircraft Co.
Talks are going on over the percentages the Korean companies might get in the project.
Taiwanese aerospace firms are also said to be interested in taking a share of the 50 percent work which would go to partners outside the AI(R) grouping.
AI(R) has shortlisted engines from General Electric and Snecma /Pratt & Whitney for the jet.

The 70-seater family would be the first new plane to be built by the AI(R) group which was formed two years as the sales and support arm of the three European companies for their existing ATR, Jetstream and Avro RJ products.
